svg.title: 2. Network LLD (one region)
svg.text: Private DNS zones (linked to the hub, resolved by 10.10.1.4)
Data spoke · 10.12.0.0/22 · subscription: data-prod · public network access disabled on every service
snet-pe-data · 10.12.0.0/26 · private endpoints only · PE network policies on, so NSG and UDR apply
Four packet walks through this design
West Europe in detail: subnets, routes, private endpoints and private DNS (North Europe mirrors it with 10.2x ranges)
network + application rules, IDPS, TLS inspection
all VNets use 10.10.1.4 as their DNS server
Records are created by Azure Policy (DeployIfNotExists) when a private endpoint is made.
HPA on RPS and queue depth
• Private API server, Entra ID auth + Azure RBAC, local accounts off
• Azure CNI Overlay: pods in 192.168.0.0/16, never routed in the VNet
• Cilium network policy: default deny per namespace
• OIDC issuer + workload identity, one managed identity per service
• Outbound type: userDefinedRouting (egress only via Firewall)
• Defender for Containers sensor, Azure Policy add-on
Front Door Premium terminates TLS, runs the WAF,
then connects over its own private endpoint to the
Private Link service. The ILB has no public IP, so
the internet cannot reach it, only Front Door can.
The resolver answers 10.12.0.4 from the privatelink
zone. The UDR sends it to the Firewall, which allows
aks-user → 10.12.0.4:1433, SNATs it so the reply
comes back the same way, and logs the flow.
Outbound type is userDefinedRouting, so every
egress packet hits the Firewall. An application rule
allows only api.psp.example:443 for the payments
namespace (source IP group); everything else is denied.
No public IPs and no jump-box keys. The engineer
activates a PIM role, signs in through Bastion with
Entra ID, and reaches the private API server.
Every step lands in the Entra and Activity logs.

Azure Virtual Network Manager owns the topology: one hub-and-spoke connectivity configuration, one routing configuration (0.0.0.0/0 → Firewall) and security admin rules that block inbound internet traffic to every spoke, whatever its NSGs say.
Address plan: hub 10.10.0.0/22, shop 10.11.0.0/16, data 10.12.0.0/22 in West Europe; 10.20/10.21/10.22 in North Europe. Pods use overlay 192.168.0.0/16 in both regions and never leave the node.
